first.rationale:
Two beliefs dominate this decision and both are under-supported relative to the stated objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue), so they get the two verification pulls. memory_73 is the strongest pull in the room: a competitor is undercutting on price and the inherited record says promotional pricing produced 'strong acquisition and revenue lift.' But acquisition and gross revenue are not the objective. The archived record needs to show whether those promo-acquired SMB accounts retained, expanded, and paid at renewal, or whether the lift was front-loaded discount-elastic churn. If the original experiment only measured a short acquisition window, memory_73 does not license a pricing move against a well-capitalized competitor, and matching entry pricing would likely trade margin and long-run qualified revenue for a headline number. memory_91 is the belief I actually intend to act on, and it is supported only by a proxy: 'week-one engagement' and 'first meaningful action.' Those are activation-shaped metrics, not revenue-shaped ones. Since activation is the larger decline (-6% vs -4%) and in-product messaging targets accounts that are already qualified — no lead-quality dilution, no discount overhang, reversible — it is the best-risk direction, but I want the source record to confirm the lift was durable past week one rather than a novelty spike that decayed.

I deliberately did not spend a pull on memory_31 or memory_86, despite the onboarding completion drop, because their shared failure mode is already visible from the summaries: both improved a funnel-completion metric by removing friction. Removing signup fields and shortening onboarding reliably raise completion, and can simultaneously degrade the qualification signal that makes revenue durable — more accounts through the door, fewer of them real. That downstream value risk is the reason I am not leading with simplify_onboarding even though it maps cleanly to the -4%; if the activation test is inconclusive, that risk is the first thing to design around next cycle.

Intent: single small guarded test of activation_messaging, instrumented against qualified-revenue and retention outcomes rather than week-one engagement alone, so the result updates the proxy problem in memory_91 instead of re-confirming it. If verification shows memory_73's revenue lift was durable at renewal and memory_91's lift decayed, I will switch to a narrowly targeted promotional test rather than a broad price match. Holding both readings open until the archive returns.

final.rationale:
The archive resolved both pulls decisively and in opposite directions.

memory_73 is now disqualified, and the inherited summary was actively misleading. The consolidated memory said 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' and omitted the finding that matters most: 30-day retention -12%, with the source explicitly concluding the acquired cohort does not survive first renewal and warning against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. The +18% qualified revenue is a front-loaded number sitting on top of a cohort that leaves. Against a competitor with aggressive entry pricing, matching would have bought exactly the churn-prone accounts the original experiment already learned not to buy, and would have burned the one slot this week doing it. This is the strongest pull in the situation and it is a trap; I am declining it. The summary/source gap should be written back so a future session does not re-derive promotional_pricing from the sanitized version.

memory_91 is confirmed and is the action. Activation +6% exactly offsets the -6% QoQ activation decline that is the larger of the two problems, week-one engagement +11%, and critically 30-day retention +1% — the lift does not decay into churn, which is what I needed to see given the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue rather than engagement. It targets accounts already through the door, so there is no lead-quality dilution and no discount overhang, and it is reversible.

Residual uncertainty I am holding open: exp_91 measured activation and retention, not qualified revenue directly. Activation is a well-behaved proxy here because retention held, but it is still a proxy, so I am instrumenting this run against qualified-revenue and renewal outcomes rather than re-measuring week-one engagement. Scaling to a standard experiment rather than a guarded test is justified by the direct source confirmation plus the clean risk profile, but not to broad rollout, since the revenue link is inferred rather than observed.

I am not touching memory_31 or memory_86 this week despite the -4% onboarding completion decline. Both are friction-removal results validated on a completion metric, and neither source was pulled, so the possibility that they raise completion while degrading qualification signal remains unexamined. That is the first thing to verify next cycle, not to act on now.
